F1_noPathWritesAbsentVerified.evidence: A sweep test drives processCityPage over every branch at once -- a real district row, a planned-development miss, a non-district raw code miss, an ordinary district miss, an unresolved token, an upstream refused cell, an upstream not-applicable cell, an upstream unaccounted cell -- for a ruled city and a no-table city, collects every cell state the job would write, and asserts the emitted kind set is exactly {value, unaccounted, refused, not-applicable}: `absent-verified` cannot appear. assertNoFalseAbsence then enforces the same invariant at runtime on every batch, and the same sweep asserts the per-parcel buckets sum to the parcel count exactly (so a parcel cannot be silently dropped either).
F1_noPathWritesAbsentVerified.deltaFromCP1sPredictedMethod: CP1 predicted a whole-file scan for the literal string 'absent-verified' in parcel-setback-cells.mjs. That test was NOT written, and this is a deliberate change of instrument, not a forgotten one: the file's own header must be able to name the state it removed (it is the defect record, and P-256's whole point is that the string's meaning was wrong, not that the word is banned), so a literal scan would either fail on prose or need an exemption rule that makes it prove nothing. The substitute is strictly stronger in the direction that matters: it asserts over EMITTED STATES, so it also catches a state assembled at runtime from a variable, which no source-string scan can.
